Competitors evolve behavioral mechanisms to minimize direct niche overlap and promote coexistence through resource partitioning. Species sharing a common food resource achieve this by feeding at different times of the day or adopting different foraging patterns on the plant.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
To avoid direct competition and coexist within the same garden, the two butterfly species may avoid competition by choosing different foraging patterns.

answer.text: increasing time spent on attacking each other

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q158 - Prion etiology of mad cow and Jacob diseases

questiontext.text: Mad cow disease in cattle and Cr Jacob disease in humans are due to infection by

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Etiological Agents in Modern Microbiology
Infectious diseases can be caused by cellular pathogens (bacteria, fungi) or acellular biological agents (viruses, viroids, and prions).

Step 2: Prion Pathogenesis
Prions are infectious agents composed solely of an abnormally folded protein lacking any genetic nucleic acid core. They induce misfolding of normal cellular prion proteins in the brain, causing transmissible spongiform encephalopathies such as bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE or mad cow disease) in cattle and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) in humans.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Mad cow disease and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease are caused by prions.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q159 - Identification of non intra uterine device

questiontext.text: Which of the following is not an Intra Uterine device?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Classification of Intrauterine Devices (IUDs)
IUDs are contraceptive devices placed directly into the uterine cavity by a medical professional. They are categorized into:
• Non-medicated IUDs (e.g., Lippes loop)
• Copper-releasing IUDs (e.g., CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375)
• Hormone-releasing IUDs (e.g., Progestasert, LNG-20)

Step 2: Nature of Progestogens
Progestogens are synthetic steroid hormones. While they serve as the active pharmaceutical agent in hormone-releasing IUDs, oral contraceptive pills, injections, and subdermal implants, progestogens themselves are hormonal compounds and not devices.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Among the given choices, progestogens are not an intrauterine device.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q160 - Matching organisms with asexual reproductive structures

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II :

List - I List - II
(a) Chlamydomonas (i) Conidia
(b) Penicillium (ii) Zoospores
(c) Hydra (iii) Gemmules
(d) Sponge (iv) Buds

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Asexual Propagules in Different Organisms
Different groups of algae, fungi, and simple animals reproduce asexually using specialized structures:
• Chlamydomonas reproduces asexually via microscopic, motile flagellated zoospores.
• Penicillium produces non-motile, exogenously formed asexual spores called conidia.
• Hydra reproduces asexually by external outgrowth known as budding.
• Sponges (e.g., Spongilla) form internal asexual buds termed gemmules.

Step 2: Pairing Analysis
• Chlamydomonas pairs with Zoospores.
• Penicillium pairs with Conidia.
• Hydra pairs with Buds.
• Sponge pairs with Gemmules.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching combination is (a) - (ii), (b) - (i), (c) - (iv), (d) - (iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q161 - Sliding filament theory and sarcomere band lengths

questiontext.text: According to the sliding filament theory:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Mechanism of the Sliding Filament Theory
The sliding filament theory describes muscle contraction through the sliding of thin actin myofilaments past thick myosin myofilaments toward the center of the sarcomere.

Step 2: Structural Changes During Contraction
• As thin filaments slide inward toward the M-line, the sarcomere shortens, decreasing the distance between successive Z-lines.
• The isotropic I-bands shorten as actin filaments overlap more deeply with myosin filaments.
• The central H-zone (the region of thick filaments not overlapped by thin filaments) narrows and disappears during maximum contraction.
• Because thick filaments do not change their physical length during this process, the anisotropic A-band retains a completely constant length throughout contraction.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
In accordance with the sliding filament theory, the length of the A-band does not change.

answer.text: Actin and myosin filaments slide over each other to increase the length of the sarcomere.
The actin filaments slide away from A-band resulting in shortening of sarcomere.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q162 - Amount of biomass produced by plants primary production

questiontext.text: The amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis is called:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle of Ecological Productivity
Ecosystem productivity describes the accumulation of organic biomass synthesized by living organisms within a defined area over a given timeframe.

Step 2: Distinction Between Productivity Terms
• Primary production is specifically defined as the total quantity of biomass or organic matter generated per unit area over a given time interval by autotrophic plants via photosynthesis.
• Gross primary productivity refers to the rate of synthesis of organic matter during photosynthesis.
• Net primary productivity represents the remaining biomass available to heterotrophs after respiratory consumption by autotrophs.
• Secondary production is the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis is called primary production.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q163 - Ionizable groups and zwitterionic structure of amino acids

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I :
Amino acids have a property of ionizable nature of \(-\text{NH}_2\) and \(-\text{COOH}\) groups, hence have different structures at different pH.

Statement II :
Amino acids can exist as Zwitterionic form at acidic and basic pH.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the Ionizable Nature of Amino Acids
An amino acid possesses an ionizable basic amino group (\(-\text{NH}_2\)) and an acidic carboxyl group (\(-\text{COOH}\)). In aqueous solution, varying the hydrogen ion concentration causes these functional groups to gain or lose protons, leading to distinct structural states (cationic, dipolar zwitterion, or anionic) at different pH values. This makes the first statement correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Zwitterionic State
A zwitterion is an electrically neutral dipolar ion bearing simultaneous positive and negative charges (\(-\text{NH}_3^+\) and \(-\text{COO}^-\)). This dipolar species predominates only at a specific intermediate pH known as the isoelectric point. In strongly acidic solutions, the carboxyl group remains protonated and the amino acid exists primarily as a net cation (\(-\text{NH}_3^+\)). In strongly basic solutions, the amino group loses its proton and the molecule exists predominantly as a net anion (\(-\text{COO}^-\)). Therefore, amino acids do not exist in the zwitterionic form at both acidic and basic pH, making the second statement incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are Incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q164 - Ciliated epithelium in bronchioles and Fallopian tubes

questiontext.text: Which of the following types of epithelium is present in the bronchioles and Fallopian tubes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural Adaptations of Epithelial Tissues
Epithelial tissues lining internal cavities are specialized to perform functions such as diffusion, secretion, absorption, or directional transport.

Step 2: Function and Distribution of Ciliated Cells
When columnar or cuboidal epithelial cells carry motile microscopic projections called cilia on their apical free surface, they form ciliated epithelium. Rhythmic beating of these cilia propels mucus and trapped particulates across the luminal surface of respiratory bronchioles toward the pharynx, and directs the ovum or zygote toward the uterus along the lumen of the Fallopian tubes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The epithelium present in both the bronchioles and Fallopian tubes is ciliated epithelium.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q165 - Endemic species restricted to Western Ghats

questiontext.text: Western Ghats have a large number of plants and animal species that are not found any where else. Which of the following term is used to notify such species?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Ecological Biogeography Terminology
Biogeographical regions with exceptional species richness and restricted distribution patterns are prioritized as biodiversity hotspots.

Step 2: Definition of Endemism
Species that are strictly confined to a specific geographical territory and not found anywhere else naturally in the world are described as endemic species. Because the Western Ghats harbor numerous native species restricted solely to this mountain range, these taxa are classified as endemics.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The term applied to species confined exclusively to a particular region is endemic species.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q166 - Gout disorder and accumulation of uric acid crystals

questiontext.text: Gout is a type of disorder which leads to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Etiology of Joint Disorders
Skeletal and muscular pathologies include autoimmune conditions, degenerative changes, and metabolic deposition disorders.

Step 2: Pathophysiology of Gout
Gout is a metabolic disorder of purine metabolism characterized by hyperuricemia. Excess uric acid precipitates as sharp monosodium urate crystals inside synovial fluid and articular tissues, triggering acute inflammation, swelling, and severe pain in the joints.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Gout leads to inflammation of joints due to the accumulation of uric acid crystals.

answer.text: Inflammation of joints due to accumulation of uric acid crystals
Weakening of bones due to decreased bone mass
Inflammation of joints due to cartilage degeneration
Weakening of bones due to low calcium level

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q167 - Definitions and lung volumes of vital capacity

questiontext.text:
Which of the following statements are correct with respect to vital capacity?

(a) It includes ERV, TV and IRV
(b) Total volume of air a person can inspire after a normal expiration
(c) The maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after forced expiration
(d) It includes ERV, RV and IRV.
(e) The maximum volume of air a person can breath out after a forced inspiration.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Definition of Vital Capacity (VC)
Vital capacity represents the maximum dynamic volume of air that can be moved into and out of the respiratory system in a single respiratory cycle.

Step 2: Component Volumes and Functional Boundaries
• Vital capacity is mathematically the sum of Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV), Tidal Volume (TV), and Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV): \(\text{VC} = \text{ERV} + \text{TV} + \text{IRV}\).
• Functionally, it is defined as the maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after a forced expiration.
• Alternatively, it is defined as the maximum volume of air an individual can exhale after a maximal, forced inspiration.
• The total volume of air inspired after a normal expiration corresponds to Inspiratory Capacity (\(\text{IC} = \text{TV} + \text{IRV}\)), not Vital Capacity.
• Residual Volume (RV) cannot be expelled voluntarily and is a component of Total Lung Capacity, not Vital Capacity.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct statements regarding vital capacity are that it includes ERV, TV and IRV; it is the maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after forced expiration; and it is the maximum volume of air a person can breathe out after a forced inspiration, corresponding to (a), (c) and (e).

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q168 - Hepatic portal system vascular connection

questiontext.text: A unique vascular connection between the digestive tract and liver is called ______.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Physiology of Portal Circulations
A portal system is a specialized vascular arrangement wherein blood collected from one capillary bed is transported through a vein to a second capillary bed before returning to the systemic venous circulation.

Step 2: Pathway of the Hepatic Portal System
In humans and other vertebrates, deoxygenated blood rich in newly absorbed nutrients and metabolites from the gastrointestinal capillaries (stomach, intestines, pancreas, and spleen) drains into the hepatic portal vein. This vein delivers blood directly into the hepatic sinusoids of the liver prior to returning to the heart via the inferior vena cava.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
This unique vascular connection between the digestive tract and the liver is known as the hepatic portal system.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q169 - Matching organs of cockroach with their functions

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the organs of Cockroach:

List - I List - II
(a) Crop (i) grinding the food particles
(b) Proventriculus (ii) secretion of digestive juice
(c) Hepatic caecae (iii) removal of nitrogenous waste
(d) Malpighian tubules (iv) storage of food

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Functional Anatomy of the Alimentary and Excretory Systems of Cockroach
• The crop is a large, sac-like expansion of the foregut used for the temporary storage of ingested food.
• The proventriculus (gizzard) possesses thick circular muscles and internal cuticular teeth that mechanically grind food particles.
• Hepatic (gastric) caecae are a ring of 6 to 8 blind tubules situated at the junction of the foregut and midgut that secrete digestive juices containing digestive enzymes.
• Malpighian tubules are thin yellow tubules located at the junction of the midgut and hindgut that function as excretory organs, extracting nitrogenous wastes from the hemolymph to convert them into uric acid.

Step 2: Pairing Associations
• Crop pairs with storage of food.
• Proventriculus pairs with grinding the food particles.
• Hepatic caecae pairs with secretion of digestive juice.
• Malpighian tubules pairs with removal of nitrogenous waste.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching sequence is (a) – (iv), (b) – (i), (c) – (ii), (d) – (iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q170 - Spirulina single cell protein and pollution reduction

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R) :

Assertion (A) :
Spirulina is a microbe that can be used for reducing environmental pollution.

Reason (R) :
Spirulina is a rich source of protein, carbohydrates, fats, minerals and vitamins.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Assertion (A)
Spirulina is a cyanobacterium cultivated on nutrient-rich organic waste materials such as wastewater from potato starch processing, animal manure, molasses, and municipal sewage. By utilizing organic effluents as substrate for rapid biomass production, its cultivation actively treats waste and reduces environmental pollution. Therefore, the assertion is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Reason (R)
Biochemical analysis confirms that dried Spirulina biomass serves as an exceptional single-cell protein source, providing up to 60–70% protein by weight, along with essential carbohydrates, lipids, minerals, and vitamins. Thus, the reason is also factually correct.

Step 3: Relationship Between Assertion and Reason
Although both statements are factually correct, the rich nutritional profile described in the reason does not explain why Spirulina reduces environmental pollution. It reduces pollution because of its ability to grow on and remediate waste organic effluents.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

answer.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q171 - Panspermia hypothesis of transfer of spores

questiontext.text: Panspermia, an idea that is still a favourite for some astronomers, means :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Historical Theories on the Origin of Life
Various scientific and historical hypotheses have been formulated to explain the origin of life on Earth, including abiogenesis, chemical evolution, spontaneous generation, and panspermia.

Step 2: Definition of Panspermia
The hypothesis of Panspermia (originally held by early Greek thinkers and favored by some modern astronomers) posits that units of life in the form of resistant microscopic spores were transferred through celestial space from other cosmic bodies or planets to Earth.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Panspermia signifies the transfer of spores as units of life from other planets to Earth.

answer.text: Creation of life from dead and decaying matter
Transfer of spores as unit of life from other planets of Earth

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q172 - Proximal to distal duct sequence in mammary gland

questiontext.text:
Arrange the components of mammary gland. (from proximal to distal)

(a) Mammary duct
(b) Lactiferous duct
(c) Alveoli
(d) Mammary ampulla
(e) Mammary tubules

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Anatomy of the Mammary Gland Duct System
Glandular tissue of each human breast is divided into 15–20 mammary lobes containing clusters of milk-secreting cells called alveoli.

Step 2: Proximal-to-Distal Route of Milk Flow
• The lumen of each alveolus opens into tiny mammary tubules.
• The tubules of each lobe converge to form a larger mammary duct.
• Several mammary ducts unite to form an expanded reservoir termed the mammary ampulla.
• The ampulla is directly connected to the lactiferous duct, through which milk is sucked out at the surface of the nipple.

Step 3: Sequential Ordering
Tracing the pathway from proximal secretory units to the distal exit gives: Alveoli → Mammary tubules → Mammary duct → Mammary ampulla → Lactiferous duct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence from proximal to distal is (c) → (e) → (a) → (d) → (b).

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q173 - Incorrect pedigree symbol for consanguineous mating

questiontext.text: Select the incorrect match regarding the symbols used in Pedigree analysis:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Standardized Symbols in Human Pedigree Analysis
In human genetics, pedigree charts use universally defined conventions:
• An unshaded diamond denotes an individual whose sex is unspecified.
• A completely filled/shaded square or circle indicates an affected individual manifesting the genetic trait.
• A square and circle joined by a single horizontal line represents normal mating between a male and a female.
• Normal parents linked to an offspring branch terminating in a shaded square represents parents with an affected male child.

Step 2: Identification of the Mismatched Symbol
Consanguineous mating (mating between close biological relatives) is designated specifically by two parallel horizontal lines connecting the male and female symbols. Representing consanguineous mating with a single horizontal line is an incorrect pairing, as a single line indicates non-consanguineous mating.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The incorrect match is the representation of consanguineous mating by a single horizontal bar between male and female symbols.

answer.text: □-○ - Parent with male child affected with disease

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q174 - Advantages of compressed natural gas over diesel

questiontext.text:
Why CNG is considered better fuel than diesel?

(a) It can not be adulterated
(b) It takes less time to fill the fuel tank
(c) It burns more efficiently
(d) It is cheaper
(e) It is less inflammable.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Environmental and Economic Merits of CNG
Compressed natural gas (CNG) was adopted as an alternative automobile fuel to curb vehicular air pollution in major urban centers.

Step 2: Evaluation of Comparative Features
• CNG burns far more completely and efficiently than diesel or petrol, leaving negligible unburnt hydrocarbon residue in the exhaust.
• Because it is delivered as a pressurized gas via dedicated pipelines, CNG cannot be siphoned off by thieves and cannot be adulterated with cheap diluents like kerosene.
• CNG is economically cheaper per kilometer compared to conventional diesel.
• Dispensing compressed gas generally requires high pressure, which does not result in faster tank fill times than liquid diesel.
• Methane is a highly flammable gas and not described as less flammable than diesel fuel.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The valid advantages of CNG over diesel are that it cannot be adulterated, it burns more efficiently, and it is cheaper, corresponding to (a), (c), (d) only.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q175 - Vector not commonly used in plant genetic transformation

questiontext.text: Which of the following methods is not commonly used for introducing foreign DNA into the plant cell?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Genetic Transformation Methods in Plants
Recombinant DNA technology uses biological vectors and physical delivery methods tailored to the cell wall properties of plant targets.

Step 2: Analysis of Transformation Systems
• Agrobacterium tumefaciens naturally transfers T-DNA from its Ti plasmid into dicot plant cells and serves as the most widely used biological vector system.
• 'Disarmed pathogen' vectors (such as disarmed Ti plasmids and plant viruses) are engineered by removing virulent genes while retaining foreign DNA delivery capability.
• The biolistic gene gun delivers high-velocity micro-projectiles coated with recombinant DNA directly through rigid plant cell walls.
• Bacteriophages are viruses specialized to infect bacterial prokaryotic cells and are not used as cloning or transformation vectors for plant cells.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The method not commonly used for introducing foreign DNA into plant cells is bacteriophages.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q176 - Pons location of respiratory rhythm pneumotaxic centre

questiontext.text: Identify the region of human brain which has pneumotoxic centre that alters respiratory rate by reducing the duration of inspiration.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Neural Control of Respiration
The basal rhythm of ventilation is generated and regulated by specialized neural clusters located in the hindbrain.

Step 2: Role and Localization of the Pneumotaxic Centre
A primary respiratory rhythm centre is located in the medulla oblongata. A second regulatory center, called the pneumotaxic centre, is situated in the pons region of the brain. Neural impulses from this pontine centre switch off the inspiratory drive, thereby shortening the duration of inspiration and consequently modifying the respiratory rate.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The region of the human brain containing the pneumotaxic centre is the pons.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q177 - Secondary spermatocytes needed for four hundred million spermatozoa

questiontext.text: How many secondary spermatocytes are required to form 400 million spermatozoa ?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Cytological Basis of Spermatogenesis
During male gamete formation in humans, primary spermatocytes (\(2n\)) undergo meiotic division I to yield two haploid secondary spermatocytes (\(n\)).

Step 2: Second Meiotic Division and Spermiogenesis
Each secondary spermatocyte undergoes equational division (meiosis II) to form two spermatids, which transform directly into two mature spermatozoa via spermiogenesis:
\[1 \text{ Secondary Spermatocyte} \xrightarrow{\text{Meiosis II}} 2 \text{ Spermatids} \rightarrow 2 \text{ Spermatozoa}\]

Step 3: Quantitative Calculation
To produce 400 million spermatozoa:
\[\text{Number of secondary spermatocytes} = \frac{400 \text{ million}}{2} = 200 \text{ million}\]

Step 4: Final Conclusion
A total of 200 million secondary spermatocytes are required to produce 400 million spermatozoa.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q178 - Intercalated discs and synchronized cardiac muscle contraction

questiontext.text: Choose the correct statement about a muscular tissue :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural Organization of Muscle Tissues
Muscular tissues are classified on morphological and functional grounds into skeletal, smooth, and cardiac muscle.

Step 2: Evaluation of Muscle Characteristics
• Skeletal muscle fibers are elongated, striated, multinucleated syncytia arranged in parallel fascicles; stating they are uninucleated is incorrect.
• Blood vessel walls are lined internally by simple squamous epithelium (endothelium) rather than columnar epithelium.
• Smooth muscle fibers are spindle-shaped (fusiform), unbranched, uninucleated, and involuntary; stating they are multinucleated is incorrect.
• Cardiac muscle cells are branched, striated cells joined end-to-end by specialized communication junctions and desmosomes called intercalated discs. These gap junctions permit ionic wave transmission so that an action potential spreads rapidly across adjacent cells, enabling the myocardium to contract synchronously as a functional unit.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct statement is that intercalated discs allow the cardiac muscle cells to contract as a unit.

answer.text: Skeletal muscle fibres are uninucleated and found in parallel bundles.
Intercalated discs allow the cardiac muscle cells to contract as a unit.
The walls of blood vessels are made up of columnar epithelium.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q179 - Follicle stimulating hormone membrane receptor and second messenger

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) :
FSH which interacts with membrane bound receptors does not enter the target cell.

Reason (R) :
Binding of FSH to its receptors generates second messenger (cyclic AMP) for its biochemical and physiological responses.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below ;

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Mechanism of Hormone Action for Peptide Hormones
Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) is a high-molecular-weight, water-soluble glycoprotein. Because it is lipid-insoluble, it cannot cross the hydrophobic core of the plasma membrane, and instead exerts its biological effects by binding to extracellular membrane-bound receptors on target ovarian cells without entering the interior. Thus, the assertion is correct.

Step 2: Generation of Second Messengers
The interaction between FSH and its specific membrane receptor activates membrane-associated adenylate cyclase, converting ATP into cyclic AMP (cAMP). This second messenger initiates a protein kinase cascade that culminates in biochemical and physiological responses. Thus, the reason is also correct.

Step 3: Relationship Between Assertion and Reason
FSH fails to enter the cell because of its lipid-insoluble, polar chemical nature, which prevents it from traversing the phospholipid bilayer. The generation of cyclic AMP describes the subsequent intracellular signaling pathway, rather than the physical reason why the hormone cannot permeate the cell membrane. Hence, the reason does not serve as the correct explanation of the assertion.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

answer.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q180 - Three chambered heart in reptilian Chelone

questiontext.text: Which of the following animals has three chambered heart ?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Comparative Anatomy of Vertebrate Hearts
Vertebrates exhibit systematic evolutionary progression in heart chamber configuration:
• Fishes have a two-chambered heart with one atrium and one ventricle.
• Amphibians and most reptiles have a three-chambered heart containing two atria and a single ventricle.
• Crocodiles, birds, and mammals have a four-chambered heart with two atria and two ventricles.

Step 2: Classification of the Given Animals
• Scoliodon (dogfish) is a chondrichthyan fish possessing a two-chambered venous heart.
• Hippocampus (sea horse) is an osteichthyan fish possessing a two-chambered heart.
• Pteropus (flying fox) is a placental mammal with a fully partitioned four-chambered heart.
• Chelone (green sea turtle) is a reptile, possessing a three-chambered heart with two atria and an incompletely divided ventricle.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The animal with a three-chambered heart is Chelone.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q181 - Elevated maternal thyroxine and pregnancy metabolic changes

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) :
During pregnancy the level of thyroxine is increased in the maternal blood.

Reason (R) :
Pregnancy is characterised by metabolic changes in the mother.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Endocrine Regulation During Gestation
During pregnancy, maternal circulating levels of several key metabolic and trophic hormones—including estrogens, progesterone, cortisol, prolactin, and thyroxine—increase substantially. Therefore, the assertion is correct.

Step 2: Maternal Metabolic Adaptation
Pregnancy entails extensive homeostatic and anabolic transformations to elevate basal metabolic rate, sustain increased blood volume, nourish placental tissues, and drive normal fetal growth. Hence, the reason is also correct.

Step 3: Relationship Between Assertion and Reason
Thyroxine is the primary regulator of basal metabolic rate in maternal tissues. The substantial elevation in maternal circulating thyroxine directly supports and drives the intense metabolic demands of gestation. Thus, the metabolic adaptations of pregnancy explain why maternal thyroxine levels increase.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

answer.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q182 - Incorrect statements regarding cyclostome morphology and spawning

questiontext.text:
Select the Incorrect statements with respect to Cyclostomes :

(a) They lack scales and paired fins.
(b) They have circular mouth with Jaws.
(c) They bear 6-15 pairs of gills.
(d) They migrate to deep sea for spawning.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Diagnostic Features of Class Cyclostomata
Cyclostomes are primitive, jawless aquatic craniates belonging to the division Agnatha.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
• The body of cyclostomes is devoid of scales and lacks paired fins.
• Respiration is carried out by 6 to 15 pairs of gill slits situated along the pharynx.
• Cyclostomes are jawless vertebrates possessing a sucking and circular mouth without jaws; asserting that they have jaws is biologically incorrect.
• Although adult cyclostomes are marine, they undergo anadromous migration to fresh water rivers and streams for spawning, rather than migrating to the deep sea; following spawning, adult cyclostomes die and their larvae return to the ocean after metamorphosis.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The incorrect statements regarding cyclostomes are that they have circular mouth with Jaws, and that they migrate to deep sea for spawning, corresponding to (b) and (d) only.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q183 - Role of tooth enamel in food mastication

questiontext.text: Role of enamel is to :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Composition and Structure of Tooth Enamel
Enamel is an acellular, highly mineralized substance covering the anatomical crown of human teeth, representing the hardest biological tissue in the human body.

Step 2: Functional Significance
The primary physiological function of this hard chewing surface is to withstand powerful compressive forces during mechanical breakdown of food, directly assisting in the mastication of food into smaller particles suitable for swallowing and enzymatic digestion.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The biological role of enamel is to masticate the food.

answer.text: Connect crown of tooth with its root.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q184 - Correct statements on connective and skeletal tissues

questiontext.text:
Choose the correct statements :

(a) Bones support and protect softer tissues and organs
(b) Weight bearing function is served by limb bones
(c) Ligament is the site of production of blood cells.
(d) Adipose tissue is specialised to store fats.
(e) Tendons attach one bone to another.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Functional Roles of Skeletal and Connective Tissues
• Bones possess a hard, non-pliable matrix that provides structural scaffolding, supporting and protecting vital soft organs and tissues.
• The long bones of the limbs serve vital weight-bearing functions and interact with attached muscles to bring about locomotion.
• Adipose tissue is a loose connective tissue located beneath the skin containing adipocytes specialized for lipid and fat storage.

Step 2: Identification of Incorrect Assertions
• Hemopoiesis (production of blood cells) occurs within the vascular red bone marrow of long and flat bones, not in ligaments.
• Tendons are dense regular connective tissues that attach skeletal muscles to bones, whereas ligaments connect one bone to another bone.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct statements are that bones support and protect softer tissues and organs, weight bearing function is served by limb bones, and adipose tissue is specialised to store fats, corresponding to (a), (b) and (d) only.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONA_MCQ_Q185 - Bivalent and tetrad formation in zygotene stage

questiontext.text: Bivalent or Tetrad formation is a characteristic feature observed during :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Pairing of Homologous Chromosomes
During the zygotene sub-stage of Prophase I in meiosis, maternal and paternal homologous chromosomes align side by side through synapsis.

Step 2: Formation of the Synaptonemal Complex and Bivalents
Synapsis is facilitated by the assembly of a tripartite proteinaceous structure termed the synaptonemal complex. The paired homologous chromosomes held together by this complex constitute a bivalent, also referred to as a four-chromatid tetrad.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Bivalent or tetrad formation is characteristic of the synaptonemal complex in the zygotene stage.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q186 - Taxonomic key features couplet and lead

questiontext.text:
Which of the following are true about the taxonomical aid 'key' ?

(a) Keys are based on the similarities and dissimilarities.
(b) Key is analytical in nature.
(c) Keys are based on the contrasting characters in pair called couplet.
(d) Same key can be used for all taxonomic categories.
(e) Each statement in the key is called Lead.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of Taxonomic Keys
A taxonomic key is an identification aid that uses a dichotomous sequence of choices based on observable similarities and differences to identify unknown organisms.

Step 2: Structural Properties of Keys
• Keys compare pairs of contrasting phenotypic characters known as a couplet, resulting in the acceptance of one condition and rejection of the other.
• Each individual statement within a taxonomic key is called a lead.
• Because identification requires systematic logical elimination, keys are analytical in nature.
• Separate, dedicated taxonomic keys are mandatory for each specific taxonomic category (such as family, genus, and species); therefore, the same key cannot be used across all taxonomic categories.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The true statements concerning taxonomic keys are that they are based on similarities and dissimilarities, they are analytical in nature, they use contrasting characters in pairs called couplets, and each statement is termed a lead, corresponding to (a), (b), (c) and (e) only.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q187 - Offspring phenotypes from carrier female and normal male

questiontext.text:
A normal girl, whose mother is haemophilic marries a male with no ancestral history of haemophilia.

What will be the possible phenotypes of the offsprings ?

(a) Haemophilic son and haemophilic daughter.
(b) Haemophilic son and carrier daughter.
(c) Normal daughter and normal son.
(d) Normal son and haemophilic daughter.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Determination of Parental Genotypes
Haemophilia is an X-linked recessive disorder where \(X^H\) represents the normal dominant allele and \(X^h\) represents the recessive mutant allele.
• The girl's mother is affected with haemophilia, meaning her genotype is \(X^hX^h\). She necessarily passes one \(X^h\) chromosome to her daughter.
• Because the girl is phenotypically normal, she must carry one normal dominant allele (\(X^H\)) from her father, giving her the heterozygous carrier genotype \(X^HX^h\).
• The male partner has no history of haemophilia, so his hemizygous genotype is \(X^HY\).

Step 2: Cross and Punnett Analysis
Crossing a carrier female with a normal male (\(X^HX^h \times X^HY\)) produces:
• Female offspring (daughters): \(\frac{1}{2} X^HX^H\) (phenotypically normal homozygous) and \(\frac{1}{2} X^HX^h\) (phenotypically normal heterozygous carrier). No daughters can inherit two mutant alleles, meaning a haemophilic daughter cannot be formed.
• Male offspring (sons): \(\frac{1}{2} X^HY\) (phenotypically normal son) and \(\frac{1}{2} X^hY\) (haemophilic son).

Step 3: Identification of Possible Phenotype Pairs
The potential offspring types generated in this mating include normal daughters, carrier daughters, normal sons, and haemophilic sons. Thus, combinations containing a haemophilic son paired with a carrier daughter, as well as a normal daughter paired with a normal son, represent genuine possible outcomes, while any combination featuring a haemophilic daughter is genetically impossible.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The possible phenotypes of the offspring are described by (b) and (c) only.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q188 - Mechanism of action of intrauterine devices

questiontext.text:
IUDs are small objects made up of plastic or copper that are inserted in the uterine cavity. Which of the following statements are correct about IUDs ?

(a) IUDs decrease phagocytosis of sperm within the uterus.
(b) The released copper ions suppress the sperm motility.
(c) IUDs do not make the cervix hostile to the sperm.
(d) IUDs suppress the fertilization capacity of sperm.
(e) The IUDs require surgical intervention for their insertion in the uterine cavity.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Mechanism of Intrauterine Contraceptive Devices (IUDs)
IUDs provide contraception by acting locally within the female reproductive tract.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
• IUDs promote a sterile local inflammatory reaction that increases (rather than decreases) phagocytosis of spermatozoa within the uterine cavity.
• Copper-releasing IUDs release copper ions that directly suppress sperm motility and impair their flagellar beat.
• In addition to impairing motility, the action of copper ions suppresses the fertilizing capacity of spermatozoa.
• Hormone-releasing IUDs alter the composition of cervical mucus to make the cervix hostile to sperm, making the claim that they do not hostile incorrect.
• IUD insertion is performed non-surgically through the vaginal canal and cervix into the uterus by a trained medical professional; it does not require surgical intervention.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct statements regarding IUDs are that released copper ions suppress sperm motility and IUDs suppress the fertilization capacity of sperm, corresponding to (b) and (d) only.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q189 - Principles of agarose gel electrophoresis of DNA

questiontext.text:
Refer to the following statements for agarose-gel electrophoresis :

(a) Agarose is a natural polymer obtained from sea-weed.
(b) The separation of DNA molecules in agarose-gel electrophoresis depends on the size of DNA.
(c) The DNA migrates from negatively-charged electrode to the positively-charged electrode
(d) The DNA migrates from positively-charged electrode to the negatively-charged electrode.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of Gel Electrophoresis
Agarose gel electrophoresis separates charged macromolecules within an electric field through a porous polymer matrix.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
• Agarose is a linear natural polysaccharide purified from seaweeds (such as Gelidium and Gracilaria).
• The porous agarose matrix exerts a molecular sieving effect; smaller DNA fragments navigate the gel pores more rapidly than larger fragments, resolving DNA fragments strictly based on their physical length or size.
• Because the phosphate backbone confers a uniform negative charge to DNA molecules, DNA fragments migrate away from the cathode (negatively-charged electrode) toward the anode (positively-charged electrode) during electrophoresis.
• The assertion that DNA migrates from the positive to the negative electrode is inverted and incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct statements concerning agarose-gel electrophoresis are that agarose is a natural polymer obtained from sea-weed, the separation depends on DNA size, and DNA migrates from the negatively-charged electrode toward the positively-charged electrode, corresponding to (a), (b) and (c) only.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q190 - Types of neurons and nerve fibres location

questiontext.text:
Match List - I with List - II :

List - I List - II
(a) Multipolar neuron (i) Somatic neural system
(b) Bipolar neuron (ii) Cerebral cortex
(c) Myelinated nerve fibre (iii) Retina of Eye
(d) Unmyelinated nerve fibre (iv) Spinal nerves

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Neurons are classified based on the number of axons and dendrites, while nerve fibres are classified as myelinated or unmyelinated based on the presence of myelin sheath formed by Schwann cells.

Step 2: Evaluation of Neural Types and Locations
- Multipolar neurons have one axon and two or more dendrites; they are typically found in the cerebral cortex.
- Bipolar neurons possess one axon and one dendrite; they are characteristically found in the retina of the eye.
- Myelinated nerve fibres are enveloped with Schwann cells that form a myelin sheath around the axon, with nodes of Ranvier between adjacent Schwann cells; they are found in cranial and spinal nerves.
- Unmyelinated nerve fibres are enclosed by Schwann cells that do not form a myelin sheath; they are commonly found in autonomous and somatic neural systems.

Step 3: Synthesis and Conclusion
Correlating the structures with their correct locations:
- Multipolar neuron corresponds to Cerebral cortex.
- Bipolar neuron corresponds to Retina of Eye.
- Myelinated nerve fibre corresponds to Spinal nerves.
- Unmyelinated nerve fibre corresponds to Somatic neural system.
This corresponds precisely to the set: (a) - (ii), (b) - (iii), (c) - (iv), (d) - (i).

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q191 - Non excretory organ in cockroach

questiontext.text: Excretion in cockroach is performed by all, EXCEPT :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Excretion in the American cockroach (Periplaneta americana) is accomplished primarily by specialized excretory structures alongside accessory excretory tissues.

Step 2: Analysis of Organs Involved in Excretion
- Malpighian tubules are the main excretory and osmoregulatory organs that extract nitrogenous waste from hemolymph and convert it into uric acid.
- Fat body cells (specifically urocytes) store uric acid.
- Uricose glands (located in the mushroom-shaped gland of male cockroaches) store and discharge uric acid.
- Nephrocytes also participate in the storage excretion of wastes.

Step 3: Identification of the Exception
Hepatic caeca (or gastric caeca) are a ring of 6 to 8 blind tubules present at the junction of the foregut and midgut that secrete digestive juices to aid in digestion. They do not perform excretory functions.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, excretion is performed by Malpighian tubules, fat body, and uricose glands, but not by hepatic caeca.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q192 - Mutation theory of evolution saltation

questiontext.text: Select the correct statement regarding mutation theory of evolution.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hugo de Vries proposed the Mutation Theory of Evolution based on his breeding experiments with the evening primrose (Oenothera lamarckiana).

Step 2: Characteristics of Mutations according to de Vries
- Unlike Darwinian variations, which are minor and directional, mutations are discontinuous, random, and directionless.
- De Vries believed that mutations arise suddenly and cause speciation in a single step, termed saltation (single step large mutation).

Step 3: Evaluation of the Statements
- The theory was proposed by Hugo de Vries, not Alfred Russel Wallace.
- Mutations are random and directionless, not small directional changes.
- Speciation occurs abruptly through single step large mutations (saltation), rather than gradual small accumulation.
- Therefore, the statement identifying single step large mutation as a cause of speciation is scientifically accurate according to the theory.

answer.text: This theory was proposed by Alfred Wallace
Single step large mutation is a cause of speciation
Large differences due to mutations arise gradually in a population

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q193 - Formed elements relative abundance in blood

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following formed elements in the decreasing order of their abundance in blood in humans :

(a) Platelets
(b) Neutrophils
(c) Erythrocytes
(d) Eosinophils
(e) Monocytes

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Quantitative Abundance of Formed Elements
In healthy adult humans, normal counts per \(\text{mm}^3\) of blood are:
- Erythrocytes (RBCs): \(5.0 \times 10^6\text{ to }5.5 \times 10^6\text{ per mm}^3\)
- Platelets (Thrombocytes): \(150{,}000\text{ to }350{,}000\text{ per mm}^3\)
- Total Leukocytes (WBCs): \(6{,}000\text{ to }8{,}000\text{ per mm}^3\)

Step 2: Abundance among Leukocyte Subtypes
The relative abundance among total leukocytes is:
- Neutrophils: \(60\%\text{ to }65\%\) of WBCs \(\approx 3{,}600\text{ to }5{,}200\text{ per mm}^3\)
- Monocytes: \(6\%\text{ to }8\%\) of WBCs \(\approx 360\text{ to }640\text{ per mm}^3\)
- Eosinophils: \(2\%\text{ to }3\%\) of WBCs \(\approx 120\text{ to }240\text{ per mm}^3\)

Step 3: Ordering from Highest to Lowest
Comparing the numbers in decreasing order:
Erythrocytes (c) > Platelets (a) > Neutrophils (b) > Monocytes (e) > Eosinophils (d).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct sequence of decreasing abundance is (c), (a), (b), (e), (d).

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q194 - Prosthetic group of catalase enzyme

questiontext.text:
The catalytic cycle of an enzyme action is given below. Identify the prosthetic group of the enzyme which catalyses the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen.

\[2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{O}_2\]

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Enzymes can be conjugated proteins (holoenzymes) composed of a protein component (apoenzyme) and a non-protein component (cofactor). Prosthetic groups are organic compounds that are tightly and permanently bound to the apoenzyme.

Step 2: Examination of the Specific Reaction
The breakdown of hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen is catalyzed by peroxidase and catalase enzymes:
\[2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Catalase}} 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{O}_2\]

Step 3: Identification of the Cofactor
In both catalase and peroxidase, the prosthetic group is haem (an iron-porphyrin complex), which forms an integral part of the active site of the enzyme.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The prosthetic group responsible for this catalytic activity is haem.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q195 - Transfer RNA anticodon sequence for UAC

questiontext.text: If the codon on m-RNA is 5' UAC 3', then identify the anticodon on t-RNA :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The mRNA codon sequence is given from \(5'\) to \(3'\) as:
\(5'\text{ UAC }3'\)

Step 2: Principles of Base Pairing and Polarity
- In RNA base pairing, Uracil (U) pairs with Adenine (A), and Cytosine (C) pairs with Guanine (G).
- During translation, codon-anticodon pairing occurs in an antiparallel orientation.
- Thus, a \(5' \rightarrow 3'\) codon pairs with a \(3' \rightarrow 5'\) anticodon.

Step 3: Determining the Anticodon Sequence
- The base complementary to \(5'\text{ U}\) is \(\text{A }3'\).
- The base complementary to \(\text{A}\) is \(\text{U}\).
- The base complementary to \(\text{C }3'\) is \(\text{G }5'\).
This produces the anticodon in the \(3' \rightarrow 5'\) direction as:
\(3'\text{ AUG }5'\)

Step 4: Writing in Standard \(5' \rightarrow 3'\) Orientation
Reversing to the standard \(5'\) to \(3'\) notation yields:
\(5'\text{ GUA }3'\)

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q196 - Endocrine regulation of kidney function statements

questiontext.text:
Regarding the control of functioning of human kidney, identify the correct statements :

(a) Angiotensin II activates the adrenal cortex to release aldosterone.
(b) Aldosterone stimulates the reabsorption of \(\text{Na}^+\) and water from the distal parts of the tubule.
(c) Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) can increase the blood pressure.
(d) Anti-diuretic hormone (ADH) can also cause vasodilation.
(e) Vasopressin is secreted from the adenohypophysis.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The regulation of kidney function involves hormonal feedback loops including the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS), Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH / Vasopressin), and Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Statement
- (a) Angiotensin II stimulates the adrenal cortex to secrete aldosterone. This statement is correct.
- (b) Aldosterone causes reabsorption of \(\text{Na}^+\) and water from the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct, maintaining blood pressure and glomerular filtration rate. This statement is correct.
- (c) Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) is released by the heart atria in response to elevated blood pressure; it induces vasodilation and natriuresis, which acts as a check on RAAS to decrease blood pressure, not increase it. This statement is incorrect.
- (d) ADH prevents diuresis and, through its constrictor effects on blood vessels (hence vasopressin), causes vasoconstriction and increases blood pressure, not vasodilation. This statement is incorrect.
- (e) Vasopressin (ADH) is synthesized in the hypothalamus and released into the bloodstream from the neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary), not the adenohypophysis (anterior pituitary). This statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Synthesis and Conclusion
Only statements (a) and (b) are factually correct statements. When combined with the regulatory mechanism context, the group containing statements (a) and (b) only forms the accurate combination.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q197 - Incorrect statement regarding metaphase chromosome

questiontext.text: Select the incorrect statement with respect to metaphase :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
During metaphase of mitosis, chromosomes reach their maximum condensation and align at the equatorial plane (metaphase plate).

Step 2: Analysis of Metaphase Features
- Spindle fibres attach to disc-shaped protein complexes called kinetochores located on the surface of the centromere.
- Metaphase is the most convenient stage to examine chromosome morphology because chromosomes are shortest and thickest.
- Chromosomes assemble along the equatorial plane forming the metaphase plate.
- Each mitotic metaphase chromosome is composed of two sister chromatids (not four) joined together at the centromere.

Step 3: Identification of the Incorrect Statement
The statement claiming that metaphase chromosomes are made up of four sister chromatids held together by the centromere is incorrect because they possess two sister chromatids.

answer.text: Spindle fibres attach to kinetochores of chromosomes.
Chromosomes are moved to spindle equator and get aligned along metaphase plate through spindle fibres to both poles.
Metaphase chromosomes are made up of four sister chromatids held together by centromere.
Complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the start of metaphase.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q198 - Incorrect statement about animal inbreeding

questiontext.text: Which of the following statement is incorrect with respect to inbreeding of animals ?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Inbreeding refers to the mating of closely related individuals within the same breed for 4 to 6 generations.

Step 2: Effects and Applications of Inbreeding
- Inbreeding increases homozygosity, which is necessary for developing pure lines in any animal breed.
- It exposes harmful recessive genes that can be eliminated through careful selection.
- It promotes the accumulation of superior alleles and elimination of less desirable genes.
- Continued close inbreeding typically leads to inbreeding depression, characterized by reduced fertility and productivity.

Step 3: Identification of the Incorrect Statement
Inbreeding systematically increases homozygosity rather than decreasing it. Therefore, asserting that inbreeding decreases homozygosity is incorrect.

answer.text: It exposes harmful recessive genes that are eliminated by selection.
Inbreeding helps in accumulation of superior genes and elimination of less desirable genes.
It is necessary if we want to evolve a pureline in any animal.

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q199 - Barriers of innate immunity matching

questiontext.text:
Match List - I with List - II :

List - I List - II
(a) Cellular barrier (i) Interferons
(b) Cytokine barrier (ii) Mucus coating of respiratory tract
(c) Physical barrier (iii) Polymorphonuclear leukocytes
(d) Physiological barrier (iv) Acid in stomach

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Innate immunity is non-specific defense present from birth and consists of four distinct barrier types.

Step 2: Evaluation of Barriers and Corresponding Examples
- Cellular barriers include specific circulating white blood cells like polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMNL-neutrophils), monocytes, and natural killer cells that phagocytose pathogens.
- Cytokine barriers are proteins such as interferons secreted by virus-infected cells to protect non-infected cells from further viral infection.
- Physical barriers form mechanical blocks against microbial entry, such as the skin and the mucus coating of the epithelium lining the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and urogenital tracts.
- Physiological barriers include secretions that hinder microbial growth, such as hydrochloric acid in the stomach, saliva in the mouth, and tears from the eyes.

Step 3: Synthesis and Conclusion
Matching each entry:
- Cellular barrier matches Polymorphonuclear leukocytes.
- Cytokine barrier matches Interferons.
- Physical barrier matches Mucus coating of respiratory tract.
- Physiological barrier matches Acid in stomach.
The correct association is (a) - (iii), (b) - (i), (c) - (ii), (d) - (iv).

name.text: NEET_UG_ZOOLOGY_2022_SECTIONB_MCQ_Q200 - Base composition in double stranded DNA

questiontext.text: In a double stranded DNA, the percentage of Adenine is 30%. What will be the percentage of Thymine and Guanine respectively ?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- DNA type: Double-stranded DNA (dsDNA)
- Percentage of Adenine (\(\text{A}\)) = \(30\%\)

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
According to Chargaff's rules for double-stranded DNA:
1. The amount of Adenine is equimolar to Thymine: \(\% \text{A} = \% \text{T}\)
2. The amount of Guanine is equimolar to Cytosine: \(\% \text{G} = \% \text{C}\)
3. The total percentage of all four bases equals \(100\%\):
\[\% \text{A} + \% \text{T} + \% \text{G} + \% \text{C} = 100\%\]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working
- Since \(\% \text{A} = 30\%\), the percentage of Thymine is:
\[\% \text{T} = 30\%\]
- The combined percentage of \(\text{A} + \text{T}\) is:
\[\% \text{A} + \% \text{T} = 30\% + 30\% = 60\%\]
- The remaining percentage represents \(\text{G} + \text{C}\):
\[\% \text{G} + \% \text{C} = 100\% - 60\% = 40\%\]
- Since \(\% \text{G} = \% \text{C}\):
\[\% \text{G} = \frac{40\%}{2} = 20\%\]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The percentages of Thymine and Guanine are \(30\%\) and \(20\%\), respectively.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2022_SECTION_A_MCQ_Q01 - Function representing non-periodic motion

questiontext.text:
Identify the function which represents a non-periodic motion.

যে অপেক্ষকটি একটি অপর্যাবৃত্ত গতি নির্দেশ করে, তা শনাক্ত করো।

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
A periodic motion repeats itself at definite, regular intervals of time, satisfying the condition \(f(t + T) = f(t)\) for a fixed non-zero time period \(T\). Conversely, a non-periodic motion does not repeat after any regular time interval and changes monotonically or decays continuously with time.

Evaluation of Functions
The sinusoidal function \(\sin \omega t\) is periodic with a fundamental time period \(T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega}\).
The sum \(\sin \omega t + \cos \omega t\) can be written as \(\sqrt{2}\sin\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\), which is also a simple harmonic periodic function with time period \(T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega}\).
The phase-shifted sine function \(\sin\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) repeats identically after every interval of \(T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega}\), making it periodic.
The exponential decay function \(e^{-\omega t}\) decreases continuously and monotonically toward zero as \(t \to \infty\). It never repeats any value at regular intervals.

Final Conclusion
The function representing a non-periodic motion is \(e^{-\omega t}\).

ধারণাগত নীতি
পর্যাবৃত্ত গতি হলো এমন একটি গতি যা নির্দিষ্ট সময় ব্যবধান পরপর পুনরাবৃত্ত হয়, অর্থাৎ একটি নির্দিষ্ট অশূন্য পর্যায়কাল \(T\)-এর জন্য \(f(t + T) = f(t)\) শর্তটি সিদ্ধ হয়। পক্ষান্তরে, যে গতি কোনো নিয়মিত সময় ব্যবধানে পুনরাবৃত্ত হয় না এবং সময়ের সাথে একমুখীভাবে হ্রাস পায় বা পরিবর্তিত হয়, তা হলো অপর্যাবৃত্ত গতি।

অপেক্ষকসমূহের মূল্যায়ন
সাইন অপেক্ষক \(\sin \omega t\) হলো \(T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega}\) পর্যায়কালবিশিষ্ট একটি পর্যাবৃত্ত অপেক্ষক।
\(\sin \omega t + \cos \omega t\) রাশিমালাটিকে \(\sqrt{2}\sin\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) আকারে প্রকাশ করা যায়, যা \(T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega}\) পর্যায়কালের একটি পর্যাবৃত্ত গতি নির্দেশ করে।
দশা পার্থক্যের সাইন অপেক্ষক \(\sin\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\)-ও প্রতি \(T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega}\) সময় অন্তর পুনরাবৃত্ত হয়, ফলে এটি একটি পর্যাবৃত্ত অপেক্ষক।
সূচকীয় অপেক্ষক \(e^{-\omega t}\) সময়ের সাথে অবিচ্ছিন্ন ও একমুখীভাবে হ্রাস পেয়ে \(t \to \infty\) সীমায় শূন্যের দিকে পৌঁছায়। এটি কখনোই কোনো নিয়মিত ব্যবধানে পুনরাবৃত্ত হয় না।

চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত
যে অপেক্ষকটি অপর্যাবৃত্ত গতি নির্দেশ করে তা হলো \(e^{-\omega t}\)।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2022_SECTION_A_MCQ_Q02 - Associated electric field of electromagnetic wave

questiontext.text:
The magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave is given by \(\vec{B} = 3 \times 10^{-8} \cos (1.6 \times 10^3 x + 48 \times 10^{10} t) \hat{j}\), then the associated electric field will be:

একটি সমতল তড়িৎচুম্বকীয় তরঙ্গের চৌম্বক ক্ষেত্র দেওয়া আছে \(\vec{B} = 3 \times 10^{-8} \cos (1.6 \times 10^3 x + 48 \times 10^{10} t) \hat{j}\), তাহলে সংশ্লিষ্ট তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্রটি হবে:

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data and Conditions
Magnetic field: \(\vec{B} = 3 \times 10^{-8} \cos (1.6 \times 10^3 x + 48 \times 10^{10} t) \hat{j}\text{ T}\)
Amplitude of magnetic field: \(B_0 = 3 \times 10^{-8}\text{ T}\)
Wave number: \(k = 1.6 \times 10^3\text{ m}^{-1}\)
Angular frequency: \(\omega = 48 \times 10^{10}\text{ s}^{-1}\)
Magnetic field direction: along \(\hat{j}\) (\(+y\)-axis)

Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The wave propagates in free space. The argument \((kx + \omega t)\) indicates propagation along the negative \(x\)-direction, i.e., in the direction of \(-\hat{i}\).
The electric field \(\vec{E}\), magnetic field \(\vec{B}\), and wave propagation vector \(\hat{c}\) form a right-handed orthogonal triad satisfying \(\hat{c} = \hat{E} \times \hat{B}\).
In a plane electromagnetic wave, the electric and magnetic fields oscillate in phase.

Relevant Formulae and Principles
Speed of the wave: \(c = \frac{\omega}{k}\)
Electric field amplitude: \(E_0 = c B_0\)
Wave propagation direction: \(\hat{E} \times \hat{B} = \hat{c}\)

Step-by-Step Working
1. Compute the propagation speed:
\[c = \frac{48 \times 10^{10}\text{ s}^{-1}}{1.6 \times 10^3\text{ m}^{-1}} = 3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}\]
2. Compute the amplitude of the electric field:
\[E_0 = c B_0 = (3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}) \times (3 \times 10^{-8}\text{ T}) = 9\text{ V/m}\]
3. Determine the direction of the electric field (\(\hat{E}\)):
Since the wave travels in the \(-\hat{i}\) direction and the magnetic field oscillates along \(\hat{j}\):
\[\hat{E} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{i}\]
Because \(\hat{k} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{i}\), the direction of the electric field is \(\hat{k}\).
4. Formulate the electric field vector:
Since \(\vec{E}\) and \(\vec{B}\) are in phase, the cosine dependence is preserved:
\[\vec{E} = 9\cos (1.6 \times 10^3 x + 48 \times 10^{10} t) \hat{k}\text{ V/m}\]

Check and Final Answer
The speed \(c = 3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}\) matches the speed of light in vacuum. The unit vector cross product confirms \(\hat{k} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{i}\), aligning with the propagation direction. Hence, the electric field is \(9\cos (1.6 \times 10^3 x + 48 \times 10^{10} t) \hat{k}\text{ V/m}\).

প্রদত্ত উপাত্ত ও শর্তাবলী
চৌম্বক ক্ষেত্র: \(\vec{B} = 3 \times 10^{-8} \cos (1.6 \times 10^3 x + 48 \times 10^{10} t) \hat{j}\text{ T}\)
চৌম্বক ক্ষেত্রের বিস্তার: \(B_0 = 3 \times 10^{-8}\text{ T}\)
তরঙ্গ সংখ্যা: \(k = 1.6 \times 10^3\text{ m}^{-1}\)
কৌণিক কম্পাঙ্ক: \(\omega = 48 \times 10^{10}\text{ s}^{-1}\)
চৌম্বক ক্ষেত্রের দিক: \(\hat{j}\) বরাবর (\(+y\)-অক্ষ)

স্বীকার্য ও চিহ্নরীতি
তরঙ্গটি শূন্য মাধ্যমে বিস্তার লাভ করছে। কোসাইন রাশির আর্গুমেন্ট \((kx + \omega t)\) নির্দেশ করে যে তরঙ্গটি ঋণাত্মক \(x\)-দিক বরাবর (\(-\hat{i}\) অভিমুখে) অগ্রসর হচ্ছে।
তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্র \(\vec{E}\), চৌম্বক ক্ষেত্র \(\vec{B}\) এবং তরঙ্গের প্রসারণ দিক \(\hat{c}\) একটি ডান-হাতি লম্ব ব্যবস্থা তৈরি করে, যেখানে \(\hat{c} = \hat{E} \times \hat{B}\)।
সমতল তড়িৎচুম্বকীয় তরঙ্গে তড়িৎ ও চৌম্বক ক্ষেত্র সমদশায় থাকে।

প্রাসঙ্গিক সূত্র ও নীতিসমূহ
তরঙ্গের বেগ: \(c = \frac{\omega}{k}\)
তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্রের বিস্তার: \(E_0 = c B_0\)
তরঙ্গ প্রসারণের দিক: \(\hat{E} \times \hat{B} = \hat{c}\)

ধাপে ধাপে সমাধান
১. তরঙ্গের বেগ নির্ণয়:
\[c = \frac{48 \times 10^{10}\text{ s}^{-1}}{1.6 \times 10^3\text{ m}^{-1}} = 3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}\]
২. তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্রের বিস্তার গণনা:
\[E_0 = c B_0 = (3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}) \times (3 \times 10^{-8}\text{ T}) = 9\text{ V/m}\]
৩. তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্রের অভিমুখ (\(\hat{E}\)) নির্ণয়:
যেহেতু তরঙ্গটি \(-\hat{i}\) অভিমুখে চলছে এবং চৌম্বক ক্ষেত্র \(\hat{j}\) বরাবর অবস্থান করে:
\[\hat{E} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{i}\]
আমরা জানি \(\hat{k} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{i}\), ফলে তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্রের অভিমুখ হলো \(\hat{k}\)।
৪. সম্পূর্ণ তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্র ভেক্টর গঠন:
যেহেতু তড়িৎ ও চৌম্বক ক্ষেত্র সমদশায় স্পন্দিত হয়:
\[\vec{E} = 9\cos (1.6 \times 10^3 x + 48 \times 10^{10} t) \hat{k}\text{ V/m}\]

যাচাই ও চূড়ান্ত উত্তর
গণনাকৃত বেগ আলোর বেগের সাথে সংগতিপূর্ণ এবং ভেক্টর গুণন দিক নির্দেশ নিশ্চিত করে। অতএব, সংশ্লিষ্ট তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্রটি হলো \(9\cos (1.6 \times 10^3 x + 48 \times 10^{10} t) \hat{k}\text{ V/m}\)।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2022_SECTION_A_MCQ_Q03 - Incorrect statement about Zener diode property

questiontext.text:
The incorrect statement about the property of a Zener diode is:

একটি জেনার ডায়োডের বৈশিষ্ট্য সম্পর্কে ভুল বিবৃতিটি হলো:

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
A Zener diode is a heavily doped \(p\text{-}n\) junction diode specifically designed to operate safely in the reverse breakdown region. Due to heavy doping of both the \(p\) and \(n\) regions, the depletion region formed at the junction is extremely thin (of the order of \(10^{-6}\text{ m}\) or less), which produces an intensely strong electric field across the junction even at low reverse voltages.

Evaluation of Statements
1. Zener voltage remains essentially constant over a wide range of reverse currents once breakdown occurs, making the diode useful as a voltage regulator.
2. A Zener diode is intentionally designed to work in the reverse bias breakdown region without undergoing irreversible damage.
3. Both the \(p\) and \(n\) semiconductor regions are heavily doped to ensure sharp breakdown at low voltage.
4. Because the diode is heavily doped, the concentration of immobile ions is very high, causing the depletion layer to be extremely narrow, not wide.

Final Conclusion
The statement claiming that the depletion region formed is very wide is incorrect.

ধারণাগত নীতি
জেনার ডায়োড হলো একটি অতিরিক্ত মাত্রায় ডোপায়িত \(p\text{-}n\) সংযোগ ডায়োড, যা বিপরীতমুখী বায়াসে ব্রেকডাউন অঞ্চলে কাজ করার জন্য প্রস্তুত করা হয়। \(p\) এবং \(n\) উভয় অঞ্চলে উচ্চ ঘনত্বের ডোপিংয়ের কারণে নিঃশেষিত স্তরের (depletion region) বেধ অত্যন্ত পাতলা হয় (প্রায় \(10^{-6}\text{ m}\) বা তার কম), যার ফলে কম বিপরীত বায়াস ভোল্টেজেই অত্যন্ত শক্তিশালী তড়িৎ ক্ষেত্র তৈরি হয়।

বৈশিষ্ট্যসমূহের মূল্যায়ন
১. ব্রেকডাউন ঘটলে বিপরীতমুখী প্রবাহের পরিবর্তন সত্ত্বেও জেনার বিভব কার্যত স্থির থাকে, যা ভোল্টেজ নিয়ন্ত্রক হিসেবে ব্যবহৃত হয়।
২. জেনার ডায়োড বিশেষভাবে বিপরীতমুখী বায়াস অবস্থায় পরিচালনার জন্য তৈরি করা হয়।
৩. তীক্ষ্ণ জেনার ব্রেকডাউন ঘটাতে এর \(p\) ও \(n\) অঞ্চল উভয়কেই উচ্চ মাত্রায় ডোপায়িত করা হয়।
৪. অতিরিক্ত ডোপিংয়ের কারণে নিঃশেষিত স্তরটি অত্যন্ত সংকীর্ণ বা পাতলা হয়, খুব চওড়া হয় না।

চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত
যে বিবৃতিটিতে বলা হয়েছে যে নিঃশেষিত স্তরটি খুব চওড়া হয়, সেটি ভুল।

answer.text: It is designed to operate under reverse bias
\(p\) and \(n\) regions of zener diode are heavily doped

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2022_SECTION_A_MCQ_Q04 - Terminal potential difference of a cell

questiontext.text:
A cell of emf \(4\text{ V}\) and internal resistance \(0.5\ \Omega\) is connected to a \(7.5\ \Omega\) external resistance. The terminal potential difference of the cell is:

\(4\text{ V}\) তড়িৎচালক বল এবং \(0.5\ \Omega\) অভ্যন্তরীণ রোধের একটি কোষকে একটি \(7.5\ \Omega\) বহিস্থ রোধের সাথে যুক্ত করা হলো। কোষটির প্রান্তীয় বিভবপ্রভেদ হলো:

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data and Conditions
Electromotive force of the cell: \(E = 4\text{ V}\)
Internal resistance of the cell: \(r = 0.5\ \Omega\)
External load resistance: \(R = 7.5\ \Omega\)

Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The cell discharges through the external resistance in a single closed circuit loop with no parallel branches.

Relevant Formulae and Principles
1. Total equivalent resistance: \(R_{\text{total}} = R + r\)
2. Circuit current (Ohm's law): \(I = \frac{E}{R + r}\)
3. Terminal potential difference across discharging cell: \(V = E - I r = I R\)

Step-by-Step Working
Calculate total resistance of the circuit:
\[R_{\text{total}} = 7.5\ \Omega + 0.5\ \Omega = 8.0\ \Omega\]
Determine the current delivered by the cell:
\[I = \frac{4\text{ V}}{8.0\ \Omega} = 0.5\text{ A}\]
Calculate the potential drop across the internal resistance:
\[V_{\text{internal}} = I r = 0.5\text{ A} \times 0.5\ \Omega = 0.25\text{ V}\]
Compute the terminal potential difference:
\[V = E - I r = 4\text{ V} - 0.25\text{ V} = 3.75\text{ V}\]
Alternatively, using the external resistance:
\[V = I R = 0.5\text{ A} \times 7.5\ \Omega = 3.75\text{ V}\]

Check and Final Answer
During discharge, the terminal voltage \(V = 3.75\text{ V}\) is strictly less than the cell's EMF (\(4\text{ V}\)), which is physically consistent. Hence, the terminal potential difference is \(3.75\text{ V}\).

প্রদত্ত উপাত্ত ও শর্তাবলী
কোষের তড়িৎচালক বল: \(E = 4\text{ V}\)
কোষের অভ্যন্তরীণ রোধ: \(r = 0.5\ \Omega\)
বহিস্থ রোধ: \(R = 7.5\ \Omega\)

স্বীকার্য ও চিহ্নরীতি
কোষটি একটি একক বদ্ধ বর্তনীতে বহিস্থ রোধের মধ্য দিয়ে তড়িৎ ক্ষরণ করছে।

প্রাসঙ্গিক সূত্র ও নীতিসমূহ
১. বর্তনীর মোট রোধ: \(R_{\text{total}} = R + r\)
২. বর্তনী প্রবাহ (ওহমের সূত্র): \(I = \frac{E}{R + r}\)
৩. ক্ষরণরত কোষের প্রান্তীয় বিভবপ্রভেদ: \(V = E - I r = I R\)

ধাপে ধাপে সমাধান
বর্তনীর মোট তুল্য রোধ গণনা:
\[R_{\text{total}} = 7.5\ \Omega + 0.5\ \Omega = 8.0\ \Omega\]
কোষ দ্বারা সরবরাহকৃত তড়িৎ প্রবাহ নির্ণয়:
\[I = \frac{4\text{ V}}{8.0\ \Omega} = 0.5\text{ A}\]
অভ্যন্তরীণ রোধে বিভব পতন:
\[V_{\text{internal}} = I r = 0.5\text{ A} \times 0.5\ \Omega = 0.25\text{ V}\]
কোষটির প্রান্তীয় বিভবপ্রভেদ:
\[V = E - I r = 4\text{ V} - 0.25\text{ V} = 3.75\text{ V}\]
বিকল্পভাবে, বহিস্থ রোধের বিভবপ্রভেদ হিসেবে:
\[V = I R = 0.5\text{ A} \times 7.5\ \Omega = 3.75\text{ V}\]

যাচাই ও চূড়ান্ত উত্তর
তড়িৎ ক্ষরণের সময় প্রান্তীয় বিভবপ্রভেদ \(V = 3.75\text{ V}\) কোষের তড়িৎচালক বল (\(4\text{ V}\))-এর চেয়ে কম, যা নীতিগতভাবে সঠিক। অতএব, কোষটির প্রান্তীয় বিভবপ্রভেদ হলো \(3.75\text{ V}\)।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2022_SECTION_A_MCQ_Q05 - Phase relationship between current and voltage in capacitor

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement-I: In an a.c. circuit, the current through a capacitor leads the voltage across it.

Statement-II: In a.c. circuits containing pure capacitance only, the phase difference between the current and the voltage is \(\pi\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

নিচে দুটি বিবৃতি দেওয়া হলো:

বিবৃতি-I: একটি এসি (a.c.) বর্তনীতে ধারকের মধ্য দিয়ে তড়িৎ প্রবাহ তার দুই প্রান্তের বিভবপ্রভেদের চেয়ে দশায় এগিয়ে থাকে।

বিবৃতি-II: শুধুমাত্র বিশুদ্ধ ধারকযুক্ত এসি বর্তনীতে তড়িৎ প্রবাহ এবং বিভবপ্রভেদের মধ্যে দশা পার্থক্য হলো \(\pi\)।

উপরের বিবৃতিগুলির আলোকে নিচের বিকল্পগুলি থেকে সর্বাধিক উপযুক্ত উত্তরটি নির্বাচন করো:

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle
When an alternating voltage \(V = V_0 \sin(\omega t)\) is applied across an ideal capacitor of capacitance \(C\), the instantaneous charge is \(q = C V = C V_0 \sin(\omega t)\). The resulting current through the capacitor is given by the time derivative of charge: \[I = \frac{dq}{dt} = \omega C V_0 \cos(\omega t) = I_0 \sin\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\] This mathematical relation demonstrates that the alternating current leads the alternating voltage across the capacitor by a phase angle of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) radians (\(90^\circ\)).

Evaluation of Statements
The assertion that alternating current leads the alternating voltage across a capacitor is physically valid.
The assertion that the phase difference between alternating current and voltage in a purely capacitive circuit is \(\pi\) is invalid, because the phase angle difference is \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) radians (\(90^\circ\)), not \(\pi\) radians (\(180^\circ\)).

Final Conclusion
Statement-I is correct but statement-II is incorrect.

ধারণাগত নীতি
যখন \(C\) ধারকত্বের একটি আদর্শ ধারকের দুই প্রান্তে একটি পরিবর্তী বিভব \(V = V_0 \sin(\omega t)\) প্রয়োগ করা হয়, তখন তাৎক্ষণিক আধান হয় \(q = C V = C V_0 \sin(\omega t)\)। ধারকের মধ্য দিয়ে প্রবাহিত তাৎক্ষণিক তড়িৎ প্রবাহ হলো আধানের সময়ের সাপেক্ষে অবকলন: \[I = \frac{dq}{dt} = \omega C V_0 \cos(\omega t) = I_0 \sin\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\] এই সমীকরণটি স্পষ্টভাবে প্রমাণ করে যে পরিবর্তী তড়িৎ প্রবাহ ধারকের দুই প্রান্তের বিভবপ্রভেদের চেয়ে \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) রেডিয়ান বা \(90^\circ\) দশায় অগ্রগামী থাকে।

বিবৃতিসমূহের মূল্যায়ন
ধারকের ক্ষেত্রে তড়িৎ প্রবাহ বিভবের চেয়ে দশায় এগিয়ে থাকে—এই উক্তিটি বিজ্ঞানসম্মতভাবে সত্য।
বিশুদ্ধ ধারকযুক্ত বর্তনীতে তড়িৎ প্রবাহ ও বিভবের মধ্যকার দশা পার্থক্য \(\pi\)—এই উক্তিটি ভুল, কারণ প্রকৃত দশা পার্থক্য হলো \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) রেডিয়ান (\(90^\circ\)), \(\pi\) রেডিয়ান (\(180^\circ\)) নয়।

চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত
প্রথম বিবৃতিটি সঠিক কিন্তু দ্বিতীয় বিবৃতিটি ভুল (Statement-I is correct but statement-II is incorrect)।

answer.text: Statement-I is correct but statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but statement-II is correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2022_SECTION_A_MCQ_Q06 - Equivalent resistance of infinite resistor ladder network

questiontext.text:
The equivalent resistance of the infinite network given below is:

নিচে প্রদত্ত অসীম বর্তনীটির তুল্য রোধ হলো:

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data and Conditions
An infinite repeating ladder network of identical resistors, each having a resistance of \(R_0 = 1\ \Omega\).
Each unit repeating stage consists of a series resistor in the upper rail (\(1\ \Omega\)), a series resistor in the lower rail (\(1\ \Omega\)), and a parallel shunt resistor connecting the two rails (\(1\ \Omega\)).

Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Because the network extends infinitely to the right, removing or adding one repeating section does not alter the total equivalent input resistance \(R_{\text{eq}}\).

Relevant Formulae and Principles
Looking to the right of the first shunt resistor, the remainder of the ladder also has an equivalent resistance equal to \(R_{\text{eq}}\).
Parallel combination of the first shunt resistor and the infinite remaining ladder: \[R_p = \frac{R_0 \cdot R_{\text{eq}}}{R_0 + R_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{1 \cdot R_{\text{eq}}}{1 + R_{\text{eq}}}\] The overall resistance across the input terminals is the series combination of the top resistor, bottom resistor, and \(R_p\): \[R_{\text{eq}} = R_0 + R_0 + R_p = 2 + \frac{R_{\text{eq}}}{1 + R_{\text{eq}}}\]

Step-by-Step Working
Set up the algebraic relation: \[R_{\text{eq}} = 2 + \frac{R_{\text{eq}}}{R_{\text{eq}} + 1}\] Multiply both sides by \((R_{\text{eq}} + 1)\): \[R_{\text{eq}}(R_{\text{eq}} + 1) = 2(R_{\text{eq}} + 1) + R_{\text{eq}}\] \[R_{\text{eq}}^2 + R_{\text{eq}} = 2R_{\text{eq}} + 2 + R_{\text{eq}} = 3R_{\text{eq}} + 2\] Rearrange into standard quadratic form: \[R_{\text{eq}}^2 - 2R_{\text{eq}} - 2 = 0\] Apply the quadratic formula: \[R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{-(-2) \pm \sqrt{(-2)^2 - 4(1)(-2)}}{2(1)} = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 + 8}}{2} = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{12}}{2} = \frac{2 \pm 2\sqrt{3}}{2} = 1 \pm \sqrt{3}\] Since electrical resistance must be positive: \[R_{\text{eq}} = (1 + \sqrt{3})\ \Omega\]

Check and Final Answer
Numerically, \(1 + \sqrt{3} \approx 2.732\ \Omega\). This is strictly greater than the series input resistors (\(1 + 1 = 2\ \Omega\)), which is physically consistent with an added positive parallel resistance. Hence, the equivalent resistance is \((1 + \sqrt{3})\ \Omega\).

প্রদত্ত উপাত্ত ও শর্তাবলী
প্রতিটি রোধের মান \(R_0 = 1\ \Omega\) বিশিষ্ট একটি অসীম ল্যাডার নেটওয়ার্ক দেওয়া আছে।
প্রতিটি পুনরাবৃত্তিক অংশে উপরের শাখায় একটি \(1\ \Omega\) রোধ, নিচের শাখায় একটি \(1\ \Omega\) রোধ এবং উভয় শাখার সংযোগস্থলে সমান্তরালে একটি \(1\ \Omega\) রোধ যুক্ত রয়েছে।

স্বীকার্য ও চিহ্নরীতি
যেহেতু বর্তনীটি অসীম পর্যন্ত বিস্তৃত, তাই প্রথম পুনরাবৃত্তিক অংশটি বাদ দিলে অবশিষ্ট অংশের তুল্য রোধও মোট তুল্য রোধ \(R_{\text{eq}}\)-এর সমান হবে।

প্রাসঙ্গিক সূত্র ও নীতিসমূহ
প্রথম উল্লম্ব রোধটির ডানদিকের অবশিষ্ট অংশের তুল্য রোধ \(R_{\text{eq}}\)।
প্রথম উল্লম্ব রোধ ও অবশিষ্ট অংশের সমান্তরাল সমবায়ের তুল্য রোধ: \[R_p = \frac{1 \cdot R_{\text{eq}}}{1 + R_{\text{eq}}}\] সুতরাং ইনপুট প্রান্ত দুটির মধ্যে মোট তুল্য রোধ হবে: \[R_{\text{eq}} = 1 + 1 + R_p = 2 + \frac{R_{\text{eq}}}{1 + R_{\text{eq}}}\]

ধাপে ধাপে সমাধান
বীজগাণিতিক সমীকরণ গঠন: \[R_{\text{eq}} = 2 + \frac{R_{\text{eq}}}{R_{\text{eq}} + 1}\] উভয় পক্ষকে \((R_{\text{eq}} + 1)\) দ্বারা গুণ করে পাই: \[R_{\text{eq}}^2 + R_{\text{eq}} = 3R_{\text{eq}} + 2\] \[R_{\text{eq}}^2 - 2R_{\text{eq}} - 2 = 0\] দ্বিঘাত সূত্রের সাহায্যে সমাধান করে: \[R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 - 4(1)(-2)}}{2} = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{12}}{2} = 1 \pm \sqrt{3}\] যেহেতু রোধের মান ধনাত্মক হতে হবে, তাই ঋণাত্মক মানটি অগ্রাহ্য করা হলো: \[R_{\text{eq}} = (1 + \sqrt{3})\ \Omega\]

যাচাই ও চূড়ান্ত উত্তর
গণনাকৃত তুল্য রোধ \(1 + \sqrt{3} \approx 2.732\ \Omega\), যা ইনপুটের শ্রেণী রোধের সমষ্টি (\(2\ \Omega\))-এর চেয়ে বৃহত্তর এবং বাস্তবসম্মত। অতএব, অসীম বর্তনীটির তুল্য রোধ হলো \((1 + \sqrt{3})\ \Omega\)।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_2022_SECTION_A_MCQ_Q07 - Maximum height attained by a projected cricket ball

questiontext.text:
A cricket ball is thrown by a player at a speed of \(20\text{ m/s}\) in a direction \(30^{\circ}\) above the horizontal. The maximum height attained by the ball during its motion is (\(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\)):

একজন খেলোয়াড় একটি ক্রিকেট বলকে অনুভূমিকের সাথে \(30^{\circ}\) কোণে \(20\text{ m/s}\) বেগে নিক্ষেপ করল। বলটির গতি চলাকালীন অর্জিত সর্বাধিক উচ্চতা হলো (\(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\)):

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data and Conditions
Initial projection speed: \(u = 20\text{ m/s}\)
Angle of projection above horizontal: \(\theta = 30^{\circ}\)
Acceleration due to gravity: \(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\)

Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Standard 2D projectile motion under uniform downward gravity, neglecting air resistance. Upward direction is taken as positive.

Relevant Formulae and Principles
Vertical component of initial velocity: \[u_y = u \sin \theta\] Maximum height in projectile motion: \[H = \frac{u_y^2}{2g} = \frac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g}\]

Step-by-Step Working
1. Compute the vertical component of initial velocity: \[u_y = 20 \times \sin 30^{\circ} = 20 \times 0.5 = 10\text{ m/s}\]
